name: sockleak
description: apple/fgx#132: a loopback descriptor must never keep a W5100 hardware socket.  An AF_INET descriptor claims one only when a verb first drives the chip (_Xport_Claim); one bound or connected to 127/8 is stamped SOCK_HW_LOOP and gives back any it holds (_Loop_ReleaseHw), which matters for the wildcard listener whose hardware listen failed after claiming.  _W5_SockAlloc hands out 1..3 only (0 is reserved for /dev/bpf0 MACRAW), so there are exactly three for the machine, and teardown skips the free for anything >= W5_NSOCK, so a sentinel stamped over a held slot strands it for the boot.  THREE RUNS, NOT TWO: each loopprobe makes two socket() calls, so a loopback path that held slots leaves the machine dry partway through the second run.  A third run costs one boot and proves the slots are genuinely recycled rather than merely sufficient for one repeat.
